title: What Intelligence Owes Marines in the Fight
gist: Podcast episode notes only: retired Lt. Gen. Mike Groen discusses intelligence support for Marines, recalling how analysis of an unfinished highway led Gen. Jim Mattis to alter the 1st Marine Division's 2003 Iraq maneuver plan, and draws on leading the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center to argue for guiding new technology with human judgment.

insights.claim: Analysis of an unfinished highway persuaded General Jim Mattis to alter the 1st Marine Division's maneuver plan during the 2003 Iraq invasion, illustrating how trusted intelligence shapes operational decisions.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Intelligence value depends on commander trust, a lesson relevant to adopting AI-driven analysis.

insights.claim: Drawing on his leadership of the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center, Mike Groen argues new military technology must be guided by human judgment and values.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Former DoD AI leadership emphasizes human-in-the-loop, shaping expectations for military AI procurement.
insights.quote: guiding new technology with human judgment and values

insights.claim: Groen prepared 3d Radio Battalion for missions in the Philippines and advanced Vince Stewart's vision for Marine intelligence.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
insights.so_what: Marine signals intelligence activity in the Philippines reflects Indo-Pacific posture.
